correctness.rationale: For N=Y⊗f the torsion coefficient is f(x)f([Y,y])-f(y)f([Y,x])-f(Y)f([x,y]); this is linear in Y for each f and vanishes on all vectors iff it vanishes on 15 basis pairs. Those equations have precisely the three explicitly described kernel spaces of dimensions 1,3,6 in all characteristics. Their projectivized constant-rank incidence strata are irreducible of dimensions 5,6,7 with distinct closures; scalar quotient pair counting gives the finite-field polynomial and the N² split. An independent brute reconstruction using 4x4 matrix-unit commutators and finite-field elimination passed all f for orders 2,3,4,5 and all nonzero f,Y for order 2. Infinite validity comes from the direct proof, not tests.

value.rationale: The standard n4 niltriangular Lie algebra is the first matrix-unit example with class three and a noncentral derived ideal, making it a meaningful boundary beyond Heisenberg and stem two-step computations. Its projective rank-one Nijenhuis locus exhibits three non-equidimensional irreducible components, arising from three different annihilator levels of the commutator filtration. The uniform finite-field census quantifies that structure for all q, including characteristic two, and distinguishes square-zero from nonsquare-zero operators. These are natural deformation-geometric and arithmetic invariants rather than a cherry-picked finite count.
